name: search_library
description: The ten paragraphs of the ministry library nearest a question in meaning, each with its id, author, work, section and text. Use it for every question about the Bible, doctrine or the Christian life. Call it once for one message of the reader's, and a second time only if their question has two distinct subjects.

question.description: The reader's question, in plain words.

name: ministry_on_verse
description: Paragraphs of the ministry library that expound one verse, best first, each with its id, author, work, section and text.

name: read_paragraph
description: One paragraph of the ministry library, whole, by its id.

id.description: The paragraph's id, from another tool's result.

name: read_verses
description: Bible verses in J. N. Darby's translation: one verse, a range within a chapter, or a whole chapter.

name: search_bible
description: Finds where the Bible says something: the verses of J. N. Darby's translation that hold the words given, at most ten of them, each with its reference and its text, and the total found. Every bare word must be in the verse; a phrase in quotes is matched as it is written. One word or one phrase comes in the Bible's order, several words best match first.

query.description: Words of the text, as shepherd or faith hope love, or a phrase in quotes, as "the grace of God".

scope.description: Where to search: OT, NT, one book by its name, as Romans, or books by their number in the Bible, as 40-43 for the Gospels. Left out, the whole Bible.

name: look_up_word
description: Articles of Morrish's Concise Bible Dictionary for a word or a subject, each with its id, headword and text.

name: app_guide
description: The sections of the app's guide on a topic: what a screen or a setting does and how to use it, step by step, and which screen to open.

topic.description: A few words, as add my own font or bookmarks.

name: open_chapter
description: Open the Bible at a chapter, or at a verse of it.

name: open_paragraph
description: Open a paragraph of the ministry library in its reader, by an id a tool gave in this conversation.

name: open_screen
description: Open a screen of the app.

name: open_dictionary_entry
description: Open an article of the dictionary, by the id look_up_word gave.

name: show_bookmarks
description: Open the reader's bookmarks.

name: get_settings
description: The reader's settings as they are now: the same fields change_settings takes.

name: change_settings
description: Change one or more of the reader's settings. Only the fields named change; a value outside its range is refused and the result says the range. themeLight lists the light themes (paper the default) and themeDark the dark ones (slate the default; those named black are true black). system follows the device between themeLight and themeDark.

themeLight.description: The light theme when theme is system.

themeDark.description: The dark theme when theme is system.

fontSize.description: The text size in px; 19 as the app comes.

paragraphs.description: Verses run on as paragraphs; off, each verse on its own line.

showNotes.description: Darby's footnote markers in the text.

noteLetters.description: Footnote letters once through the chapter, or restarting on each printed page.

moreColours.description: Offer twelve highlight colours instead of four.

motionSpeed.description: Animation speed; 1 as the app comes.

align.description: Where the column sits on a wide screen.

width.description: How wide the column may grow on a wide screen.

ttsWord.description: Light each word as it is read.

ttsAutoNext.description: Go on to the next chapter when one ends.

name: start_listening
description: Read a chapter aloud, from a verse if one is given; with no reference, the chapter the reader is at.

name: stop_listening
description: Stop reading aloud.

name: add_bookmark
description: Bookmark a verse, or a whole chapter.

name: add_highlight
description: Highlight a verse or a range of verses within a chapter in a colour.

name: list_jottings
description: The reader's own {nouns}, newest first, each with its id, its title and the day it last changed: at most fifty, and how many there are in all. With words, only those that hold every word, in the title or in a line. For one the reader names, call read_jotting with its title instead.

words.description: A few words to find, as prayer. Leave out for the newest fifty.

name: read_jotting
description: One of the reader's own {nouns}: its title and its lines, each with its number, and `updated`, which edit_jotting takes to replace, remove or move a line. Give its id, or, when the reader names one ("my {noun} on prayer"), words of its title: do not list first. One that matches is read; several are given by id and title, to read by id; none says so. A long one is cut at 12,000 characters and says so.

title.description: Words of its title, as prayer.

name: open_jotting
description: Open one of the reader's own {nouns} on the screen, by its id.

name: create_jotting
description: Make a new private {noun} for the reader from a title and its lines: passages by reference, notes, links, headings, and paragraphs of the library by the id a library tool gave, which the app writes as a link to that paragraph. A note that says what a writer of the library wrote names that writer, one writer to a note, and is followed by the paragraph line it rests on: give a writer no words without one. The reader's own words need none. At most 60 lines, a note at most 2,000 characters; keep the call short, and add more with edit_jotting. Every passage must be a real chapter, or verses of one chapter. If any line is refused nothing is made, and the result says which line and why. The result says whether it was made: made at once, made when the reader tapped Apply on what the app showed them, or not made.

reference.description: For a passage: a chapter or verses of one chapter, as Romans 8:1, John 3:16-18 or Psalm 23.

text.description: A note's or a heading's words, or a link's label. A passage has none.

url.description: For a link: an http or https address.

paragraph.description: For a paragraph: its id, as a library tool gave it.

depth.description: How far the line sits under the one above: 0 as a line comes.

name: edit_jotting
description: Change one of the reader's own {nouns}: add lines, replace, remove or move lines, or give it another title. A line is as create_jotting takes one. Every line number is the line's number as read_jotting gave it, before this edit. To replace, remove or move a line, or to add one after a line by its number, give `updated` as read_jotting gave it; to add at the end or at the top (after 0), or to rename, no reading is needed. Put everything you change in one {noun} from one reading into one call: once a call has changed it, the numbers of that reading are refused. If any part is refused nothing is changed, and the result says why. The result says whether it was changed: at once, when the reader tapped Apply on what the app showed them, or not at all.

updated.description: As read_jotting gave it. Needed to replace, remove or move, and to add after a line by its number.

after.description: The number of the line to add it after, as read_jotting gave it; 0 for the top. Leave out to add at the end.

line.description: The number of the line to replace.

remove.description: The numbers of the lines to take out.

line.description: The number of the line to move.

after.description: The number of the line to put it after; 0 for the top.

name: draft_feedback
description: Open the feedback form with a message to the developer filled in. The reader reads it, changes it if they wish, and sends it themselves; this sends nothing.
